la:noun:Byzantium.html:
Bȳzantĭum, ii, n., = Βυζάντιον,
a city in Thrace, on the Bosphorus, opposite the Asiatic Chalcedon, later Constantinopolis, now Constantinople; among the Turks, Istamboul or Stamboul (i.e. εις τὴν πόλιν), ; ; sq.; ; ; ; . 83; 3, 47 al.—
Derivv.
Bȳzantĭus, a, um, adj., of Byzantium, Byzantine: litora,the Strait of Constantinople,: portus,.—Subst.: Bȳ-zantĭi, ōrum, m., the inhabitants of Byzantium, ; sq.; ; ; .—
Bȳzantĭăcus, a, um, adj., of Byzantium: lacerti,. —
Bȳzantīnus, a, um, adj., the same (post-class.): Lygos,: frigora,.

la:noun:byssus.html:
byssus, i, f. (byssum, i, n., ), = βύσσος [Heb. ],
cotton, cotton stuff, ; ; (acc. to others, a fine kind of flax, and the linen made from it; v. Liddell and Scott's Lex.).
